transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um… I guess what finally made me come in is this thing that keeps happening at work. In longer sales strategy meetings, I find myself getting up when I know I’m supposed to just stay seated—like, I’ll go refill my water or kind of pace near the printer. It’s not like I’m trying to be disruptive, I just… have a hard time staying put for the whole meeting. Is that the kind of thing that’s worth talking about?
Do you find yourself feeling restless or having trouble staying still in other situations outside of work?

I guess the clearest example is still those longer strategy meetings at work… I keep getting up even when I know I’m supposed to stay seated. Like I’ll tell myself I’m just refilling my water, or I’ll sort of pace by the printer for a minute. It’s not terrible, I don’t think, but it happens enough that I noticed it and felt like I should probably mention it.
Do you often feel restless when you're not in a meeting?

Um… outside of meetings, I’m not totally sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed it in a big obvious way. Maybe I get a little fidgety sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s more than anyone else, if that makes sense. The meeting thing is the main one I can point to.
Do you have any habits or thoughts that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?

Um… no, I don’t think so. Not in the sense of, like, needing to repeat a thought or a ritual over and over. I mean, I might double-check something normal, like anyone would, but nothing that feels compulsive or like I can’t stop. Is that what you mean?
Do you often feel anxious or worried about things in your daily life?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’m an especially anxious person, I don’t think. I worry about normal day-to-day stuff sometimes, like anyone would, but it doesn’t feel like it’s taking over or anything. At least, I don’t think so. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you find that you worry about things more than your friends or family?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, some of my friends seem way more worried about things than I am, honestly. I definitely worry here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s more than other people. At least not that I’ve noticed.
Do you often feel nervous or anxious in social situations, like when you're with coworkers or in a group of people?

Not really, no. I mean, I can feel a little awkward sometimes in a group if I don’t know people well, but I think that’s pretty normal? With coworkers I’m usually fine. I wouldn’t say I’m, like, nervous or anxious in social situations in a big way.
Do you often find yourself preoccupied with worries about everyday things, even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Not really, I don’t think. I mean, if something specific is going on, I might think about it, but I don’t usually sit around worrying for no reason. At least, I haven’t noticed that being a big issue.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?

Um… sometimes, yeah. I try not to, but I do catch myself jumping in before someone’s even finished asking a question, especially with clients or coworkers. Like I think I know where they’re going, so I answer, and then I realize I cut them off or answered the wrong thing. It’s not constant, but it does happen enough that I notice it.
Do you often act on impulse in your personal life, outside of work?

I don’t think so, not in any major way. I mean, I probably do little things without fully thinking them through sometimes, like anyone does, but nothing that really stands out to me as a big problem. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you often interrupt others or blurt out answers in your personal relationships?

Yeah… I guess I do that a little. Not like I’m trying to be rude, but if someone is talking through something or working through a presentation, and I suddenly think of an idea, I’ll kind of jump in or pop over to add it. Sometimes I realize afterward it probably could’ve waited. I try to frame it as being helpful, but… yeah, I can see how it might be interrupting.
Do you think your tendency to interrupt or blurt out answers has caused any problems in your personal relationships?

I don’t think it’s caused any serious problems, no. Maybe little moments where someone looks annoyed or says, “Let me finish,” and then I feel bad and apologize. But I don’t think it’s damaged any relationships or anything like that… at least not that I’m aware of. Is that what you mean?
Do you often act on impulse in situations where it's not expected or appropriate?

I mean… not usually in a really inappropriate way, I don’t think. But yes, sometimes if I’m in the middle of a conversation or someone’s working through a deck and I suddenly have an idea, I’ll kind of jump in or pop over to add it. In my head it feels helpful, but afterward I can see that maybe it wasn’t the right moment and it probably could’ve waited.
Has your tendency to act on impulse or interrupt others ever caused you significant distress or problems?

I mean… “significant” feels like a strong word, but yeah, it has started to worry me more at work. It’s come up in performance reviews in kind of a polite way, like needing to be more mindful about timing or letting people finish.

And there was one client complaint that really got to me. I don’t think I meant anything badly at all — I really do care about doing good work and keeping clients feeling heard — but it made me realize that if I jump in too much or act too fast, it could actually affect trust or even damage an account. So… yeah, I guess it has caused me distress, even if I’ve tried to downplay it.
Do you have more trouble with paying attention to details or with waiting for your turn to speak or act?

Probably waiting my turn, if I’m being honest. I do try to be polite, but on client calls or in office discussions I can get really restless waiting for the right opening. I’ll check the clock or kind of rehearse what I want to say in my head, and then sometimes I just jump in too early.

I don’t mean to be rude — it’s more like I’m afraid I’ll lose the thought or miss the moment. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you think you have more trouble sitting still and focusing, or with controlling your impulses and waiting for the right moment to act?

I think it’s more the impulse and waiting-for-the-right-moment part. I can sit still when I need to, mostly, but on client calls or in office discussions I get kind of restless waiting for my turn.

I’ll be checking the clock or rehearsing what I want to say so I don’t lose it, and then… sometimes I just come in too early. I don’t mean to steamroll anyone, but that’s probably the piece I have the harder time managing.
